subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the focused global/per-binding `groupScope` contract from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91702, or first define a general canonical shared-session binding contract for groups, channels, and threads?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability gap, but both choices alter public config, session identity, queue serialization, reply routing, and privacy boundaries; repository evidence cannot determine the intended permanent API.

options.title: Adopt focused groupScope
options.body: Approve the backward-compatible group-to-main scope, require isolated defaults, origin-safe delivery, security diagnostics, documentation, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Design canonical shared sessions
options.body: Pause the focused PR and consolidate this issue with broader named-session routing work before adding a public config surface.

options.title: Retain isolation
options.body: Decline group-to-main folding and keep explicit memory or cross-session tools as the supported context-sharing mechanisms.

recommendation.title: Adopt focused groupScope
recommendation.body: Approve the backward-compatible group-to-main scope, require isolated defaults, origin-safe delivery, security diagnostics, documentation, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest sustained history across the routing decision surface, outbound thread behavior, and session documentation makes this the best available owner for the product-boundary choice.
